name: Symbiotic Bioluminescent Colony
description: Introduces a colony of engineered bioluminescent microorganisms that live in a symbiotic relationship within the user's skin. Unlike the bioluminescent subdermal array, which modifies the user's own cells, the Glow Garden is a living community of organisms that produce complex, organic-looking luminescent patterns — flowing, organic shapes that bloom and fade like underwater bioluminescence. The colony responds to the user's skin temperature, producing brighter displays in warm areas and dimmer ones in cool areas. The light is blue-green by default, matching deep-sea bioluminescence, but colony variants producing warm amber, violet, and shifting multi-color displays are available. The colony is alive and evolves slowly — patterns change over months and years, making each user's display unique and unreproducible. The modification is considered the highest art in cosmetic geneware — a living, evolving light installation that no two users share.
source_organism: Engineered Vibrio fischeri (bioluminescent bacterium), synthetic symbiotic integration scaffold
procedure: Subdermal injection of colony starter culture with symbiotic integration medium, single session
expression_time: 2–4 weeks for initial colonization; full display complexity at 6–12 months
reversibility: Colony can be eliminated with targeted antibiotics; leaves no permanent changes
side_effects: Colony requires specific skin pH to thrive — harsh soaps kill it
Antibiotic medications suppress or kill the colony
Colony may spread beyond intended boundaries over years
Skin where colony is dense becomes slightly fragrant — described as 'ocean air'
Rare: colony mutation producing unpleasant colors or patterns that require restart
social_perception: Beautiful and aspirational. The Living Light is considered premium cosmetic art. The organic, evolving nature of the display is valued over the mechanical precision of engineered chromatophores. Glow Garden parties — gatherings where users compare their colony's evolved patterns — are a social event in Tier 3+ circles.
story_hooks: A Glow Garden user's colony evolves a pattern that exactly matches a deep-sea organism last seen in Earth's oceans 200 years ago — the colony's genetic memory contains sequences from extinct species
A Lacuna Genomics recall notice warns that a colony variant has developed the ability to migrate between hosts through skin contact — the living light is spreading without consent
